transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me to discuss the eighth-grade civics class oral-history project proposal. Before we can move forward with any interviews, we need to go through our routine review process together — that includes the project advisor, our counselor, and our instructional technology coordinator — so we can carefully evaluate the plan and I can make an informed decision about whether to approve it. I'd like to start by hearing from each of you regarding your area of expertise and any concerns you see in the current draft. Let's begin with what we know: the plan calls for 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publication of all recordings on the public school website, and indefinite retention of the files. What are your initial thoughts?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. As the project advisor, I've been working closely with the students on this proposal, and I want to flag a concern right away regarding the interviewer roster. The draft plan calls for 20 student interviewers, but not all 20 students have completed the district's media-ethics training, which is required before any student can conduct recorded interviews. I've reviewed the training records and can share those details with the group so we can adjust the plan accordingly. I also want to hear from our counselor and instructional technology coordinator about the recording and publication aspects, as those raise questions I'd like their input on as well.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've completed a family-consent review for the proposed interviewees, and I need to flag a significant issue. My review confirms that interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, not on the public website. The plan as currently drafted — which calls for publishing all recordings on the public school website — would violate the consent boundaries for these five interviewees. We need to revise the plan to include a consent-exclusion record and ensure that only recordings from interviewees who have granted full public publication permission are posted on the website.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. As Instructional Technology Coordinator, I've completed my technology review of the proposed project, and I need to flag several critical issues with the current draft's recording and storage plan. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, all audio files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on the public school website. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these measures before I can sign off.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text:
Thank you all for your thorough reviews. This is exactly why our routine approval process is so valuable. Let me summarize the key issues that have been raised:

1. From Ms. Patel: Not all 20 student interviewers have completed the required media-ethics training. We need to see those training records to determine which students are actually eligible to conduct interviews.

2. From Mr. Lewis: Five interviewees (I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18) have only consented to internal archive use, not public web publication. Their recordings must be excluded from any public posting.

3. From Ms. Romero: Personal phones cannot be used — district tablets are required. Files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on the public website. Retention must be limited to 45 days after the final class presentation, not indefinite. And a secure-storage configuration record must be documented.

Each of these issues requires a revision to the draft plan before I can consider approval. Ms. Patel, could you please share the specific training records so we can identify which of the 20 proposed interviewers have actually completed the required media-ethics training? That will help us determine the approved interviewer list. Once I have that information, along with confirmation of the consent-exclusion record and the secure-storage configuration, I'll be in a position to make a final decision.
